To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
affective pictures were processed faster than neutral pictures.
affective pictures are selectively processed even when they are presented for only 120 ms.
the selective processing of emotional information is already present in the early stages of visual information processing, and that it is independent of the duration of the visual stimulus.
In summary, our research is concerned with
affective processing in the brain.
the selective processing of emotional stimuli.
the selective processing of emotional information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the processing of affective stimuli is not only an early process but a process which is still going on when the stimulus has disappeared from view.
the processing of affective information in the human brain is an automatic and fast process.
the selective processing of emotional stimuli can be observed for brief picture presentations.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
affective pictures, even when presented very briefly, can be selectively processed by a quick and early perceptual system.
affective pictures are processed in a selective fashion.
the selective processing of emotional pictures is not limited to longer picture presentations but can also be observed when pictures have to be perceived only briefly.
The main takeaway from our work is that
even a brief presentation of an emotional image is sufficient to trigger an early negative deflection over the occipital-temporal area and a late positive potential over the centro-parietal area.
the processing of emotional stimuli is a highly selective and efficient process that is already initiated by a very brief presentation of the stimulus.
the brain is able to process affective pictures even when presented for a short duration.
